{ "rules": [
    "Model forecasts are consistently too low in the early horizon and too high in the long horizon, showing lag and overshoot that violates mean reversion expectations",
    "Sentiment positively correlates with price changes but model forecasts underweight this relationship, especially when sentiment shifts from negative to positive",
    "When price history shows a clear uptrend, model forecasts lag behind true outcomes by 0.3-0.8 points per day for the first 5-10 forecast horizons",
    "Mean reversion bias: model maintains levels too far from recent prices, especially at 10-20 day horizons where true outcomes show more rapid convergence to mid-range values",
    "Sentiment strength matters: high sentiment (0.67-1.00) zones in examples 1-5 show model forecasts that are 0.3-0.7 points too low compared to true outcomes",
    "When sentiment turns negative (0.00-0.33), model forecasts remain too optimistic by 0.2-0.5 points per day relative to the mean-reverting price correction",
    "Cross-horizon consistency violation: values at 5-day and 25-day horizons in model forecasts move in opposite directions to true outcomes 15-20% more than expected" ]}
